Both deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) models were outperformed by the proposed dual-branch CNN with shared weights. With an accuracy of 97.26%, precision of 99%, recall of 99.27%, and an F1 score of 98.88%, this model has achieved a remarkable performance.

title: Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence, and Crisis Response Outcomes in European Public Administration: A Systematic Review and Future Research Agenda
abstract: The rising number and the complexity of crises in Europe, including the COVID-19 pandemic, migration, and cybersecurity threats, have accelerated the adoption of digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) in public administration. This paper is a systematic literature review (SLR) of 58 academic sources examining the effect of digital transformation and AI on crisis response outcomes in European public administration. Records were identified in Scopus and Web of Science, complemented by supplementary sources, and critically appraised through a two-step procedure based on the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. The review integrates major themes such as the evolution of digital governance, AI-enabled decision-making, performance in crisis management, and institutional resilience. Gains in efficiency, coordination, and responsiveness are widely reported, but the appraisal shows that they rest on a thin evidential base&mdash;one quasi-experimental study, no longitudinal designs, and twenty non-empirical records&mdash;while governance, accountability, ethical, and institutional-capacity problems persist. The article reveals significant gaps in research and suggests a broad research agenda in the future with emphasis on theoretical, methodological, and policy aspects. The paper contributes to the emerging digital-era governance literature and offers recommendations for policymakers and researchers.

title: Interpretable Subgroup Discovery with Abstention in Small, Heterogeneous Clinical Trials: A Retrospective Multi-Dataset Study
abstract: Small, heterogeneous clinical datasets pose a challenge for whole-cohort prediction because clinically meaningful treatment or response patterns may be diluted across biologically diverse patients. We describe and evaluate NetraAI, an interpretable dynamical-systems framework for selective subgroup discovery that uses finite-iteration contraction-inspired dynamics and long-range memory (LRM) to identify stable, outcome-linked Model-Derived Subgroups (MDS). This system can abstain by assigning No Call when a stable subgroup assignment is not supported. A large language model (LLM) Strategist is outlined only as a possible future extension; it is not evaluated here and contributes nothing to the results reported. Foundation and language models asked to perform subgroup discovery directly did not recover the structure the specialized discovery step recovered. We demonstrate this framework across three retrospective clinical trial datasets: Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness (CATIE) schizophrenia (olanzapine vs. perphenazine comparative treatment-preference benchmark), Canadian Biomarker Integration Network in Depression (CAN-BIND) depression (escitalopram response), and Comprehensive Molecular Characterization of Advanced Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma for Better Treatment Selection (COMPASS) pancreatic cancer (GnP vs. FOLFIRINOX observational regimen-associated response). The benchmark is not a contest between NetraAI and competing predictors: the same eight downstream methods are evaluated with and without what NetraAI discovered. Given the full feature sets and their own selection procedures, those methods were at or near chance on all three datasets, and blind de novo searches by an independent interaction model and by a pretrained tabular foundation model did not recover an equivalent signature or subpopulation. In internal downstream evaluation, given the discovered variables alone&mdash;the same patients, the same classifiers, the full cohort and no abstention of any kind&mdash;every one of the eight methods improved on every dataset, 24 of 24 method-dataset comparisons, moving from a raw-feature range of 0.46&ndash;0.62 AUC to 0.54&ndash;0.78. Restricting further to the subpopulation in which those variables hold improved all eight methods again in CAN-BIND and in COMPASS, 16 of 16 comparisons, reaching 0.66&ndash;0.83 and 0.96&ndash;1.00, respectively; in CATIE, where the called subgroups are the least outcome-homogeneous of the three, it improved only one of eight. Taking the framework as a whole, 23 of 24 method-dataset combinations improved over the raw-feature baseline. NetraAI abstains on patients without stable subgroup structure, calling 27.7% to 40.4% of each cohort. The contribution demonstrated is therefore subgroup discovery rather than downstream prediction, and its beneficiaries are the conventional methods themselves. In COMPASS, NetraAI identified a three-SNV signature associated with regimen-linked response ranking among called patients; because the cohort was observational and the permutation test was conditional on the selected signature, this finding is exploratory. The two mechanisms are complementary rather than competing: variable discovery establishes which features carry the structure, and abstention establishes in which patients it holds. Neither mechanism replaces conventional modeling. Variable discovery improved every method on every dataset, the pretrained tabular foundation model included; identifying the population in which those variables hold conferred further benefit in two of the three datasets and not in the third. These findings support NetraAI as an exploratory system for generating compact, inspectable subgroup hypotheses that may inform future enrichment strategies after external validation, and indicate that its value lies in what it contributes to other methods rather than in competing with them.

title: HDPF: Hierarchical Dual-Perspective Collaborative Modeling for Multimodal Image Fusion
abstract: Different imaging modalities exhibit inherent discrepancies in intensity characteristics and information representation, resulting in pronounced heterogeneity among multimodal features. When these heterogeneous features are directly learned and fused within a unified representation space, feature coupling may arise, leading to mutual interference between global structural information and local fine-grained details. To address the limited differentiated modeling of structural and fine-grained information in existing methods, we propose Hierarchical Dual-Perspective Collaborative Modeling for Multimodal Image Fusion (HDPF). HDPF employs a Dual-Perspective Feature Aggregation Block (DFAB) to jointly exploit convolution-based local representation and Transformer-based global contextual modeling. Building upon this dual-perspective representation, HDPF further constructs two differentiated pathways dedicated to structural information and detail information, respectively, thereby providing differentiated representations of complementary multimodal information. The extracted features are subsequently reorganized and integrated by the decoder to reconstruct the final fused image. Extensive experiments are conducted on multiple infrared&ndash;visible image fusion (IVF) datasets as well as medical image fusion (MIF) tasks. On the TNO dataset, HDPF achieves VIF and MI scores of 0.80 and 3.50, respectively. On the MRI&ndash;PET fusion task, the VIF score reaches 0.61. The experimental results demonstrate that HDPF achieves competitive and relatively balanced fusion performance across the evaluated multimodal image fusion tasks.

title: Accountable Autonomy: A Governance Framework for Agentic AI in Telecommunication Networks
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed across distributed cloud&ndash;edge&ndash;radio infrastructures, where autonomous agents make decisions with direct operational and economic impact. Smart contracts (SCs) enforce business rules and policies, constraining autonomous actions according to predefined operational intent. As agent autonomy expands across heterogeneous networks, ensuring accountability requires transparency, verifiability, and compliance with SC-defined requirements. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Agent Governance Framework (AGF), which integrates SC-based governance into agentic AI systems, enabling verifiable accountability through traceable autonomous decisions. Built on European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) and TM Forum principles, AGF comprises six components: (i) a TM Forum-aligned business support system (BSS); (ii) an agentic AI-enhanced operations support system (OSS); (iii) a Network Resource Operations subsystem; (iv) an Identity and Access Role Manager; (v) a Distributed Marketplace; and (vi) a Traceability and Auditability Registry. Together, these components provide an end-to-end (E2E) traceable architecture, linking each action to the responsible agent and SC. A prototype on a local test network with the evaluation of two complementary network test cases demonstrates the framework&rsquo;s feasibility, confirms its full traceability and immutability, and highlights AGF&rsquo;s potential as a foundation for reliable, large-scale agent-based systems in telecommunications networks. The results demonstrate 100% traceability across the E2E governance loop and a minimal latency overhead of 2&ndash;4% due to the Traceability and Auditability registry.

title: Evaluating Explainable Hybrid Intrusion Detection Models Under Zero-Day Conditions
abstract: Zero-day network attacks pose a significant threat because their unknown signatures evade traditional detection mechanisms. This research develops an AI-enhanced intrusion detection system that aims to detect such attacks while providing interpretable outputs for security analysts. Four machine-learning models are evaluated under strict zero-day conditions using two benchmark datasets. SHAP and LIME are applied to produce instance-level explanations, and a formal stability assessment is conducted to determine their reliability. Experimental results show that the hybrid model combining anomaly-based detection with deep learning achieves the highest zero-day Recall, with statistically significant advantages over individual models in detecting previously unseen attacks, while the standalone LSTM achieves the strongest overall balance between Precision and Recall. The generated explanations consistently reveal security-relevant features, and stability analysis confirms their robustness across conditions. The study demonstrates that integrating deep learning with stable explainable AI offers a practical and trustworthy solution for zero-day intrusion detection, contributing validated evidence to an area where explanation reliability is rarely examined.

title: Forecasting Gas-Dynamic Processes and Phenomena in Coal Mines Using Ensemble Model of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Predicting emergencies caused by uncontrolled and sometimes sudden changes in methane concentration within working and adjacent zones of coal mines remains a critical and challenging task, the solution for which can greatly enhance mining safety. This study presents a hybrid machine-learning model trained on real and synthetic data for accurate methane concentration forecasting and risk-level classification. The authors propose an ensemble method comprising staged data preprocessing, generation of physically meaningful features, and weighted ensembles for both regression and classification. The system is augmented with expert rules to correct forecasts and a built-in anomaly detection mechanism based on residual analysis. Experimental evaluation confirmed the model&rsquo;s high performance: for regression, the coefficient of determination reached 0.984&ndash;0.997; the classifier achieved a recall of 92.8% for the rare &ldquo;Accident&rdquo; class under severe data imbalance (10:1). The ensemble approach reduced error variance by 40&ndash;60% compared to baseline models. The results indicate the feasibility of pilot application for dynamic early warning, which can substantially reduce coal mine accident risks.

title: Generalizable Deepfake Detection via Frequency-Domain Enhancement and Feature Disentanglement
abstract: Existing deepfake detectors often perform well on in-domain data but generalize poorly to unseen datasets or manipulation methods. This limitation is largely attributed to their reliance on dataset-specific semantic cues rather than transferable forgery patterns. To address this limitation, we propose a generalizable deepfake detection framework that combines frequency-domain enhancement with feature disentanglement. A Phase-Amplitude Frequency Enhancement (PAFE) module enhances subtle spectral artifacts introduced during deepfake generation. We then feed the enhanced representations into an asymmetric dual-branch architecture that separates content-related information from forgery-related features. The content branch models facial semantics, while the forgery branch extracts discriminative forgery features with reduced content interference. A spatial self-attention module further refines the forgery features. We optimize the framework using image-level reconstruction loss, feature-level contrastive loss, and classification loss. Together, these objectives encourage effective feature disentanglement and improve the discriminability of the learned forgery features. Extensive experiments on several widely used deepfake benchmarks show that the proposed framework achieves competitive detection performance and improved cross-domain generalization compared with existing methods.

title: From Prediction to Decision Support: A Critical Review and Six-Layer Framework for Responsible Artificial Intelligence in Sport Science
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in sport science to classify movement, analyse tactics, estimate readiness, forecast performance and injury risk, and support rehabilitation. Predictive performance alone, however, does not establish practical usefulness, safety, or responsible use. Through purposive source selection and critical synthesis, this review integrates sport-specific evidence with guidance on prediction modelling, human&ndash;AI interaction, and AI risk management. It highlights five recurring gaps: limited data and labels; leakage-prone or temporally inappropriate validation; weak reporting of calibration and uncertainty; unclear translation from prediction to action; and insufficient attention to athlete rights and post-deployment monitoring. We propose a six-layer framework covering data and context, prediction, decision translation, individualisation, human oversight, and deployment monitoring. For each applicable layer, the framework specifies evidence to document, appraisal questions, and common failure modes. It distinguishes model development from operational decision support and links technical evaluation with workflow utility, fairness, privacy, accountability, contestability, and lifecycle governance. The framework is conceptual, not a validated scoring or certification instrument. Sport-science AI should be evaluated as a socio-technical intervention rather than an isolated algorithm. Future studies should prioritise athlete-level and temporal validation, calibrated probabilities, external and prospective evaluation, prespecified action pathways, subgroup performance, documented override procedures, and ongoing monitoring.

title: A Quantum-Memetic Hybrid Framework for Combinatorial Optimization: Synergistic Integration of Superposition-Based Exploration with Adaptive Exploitation
abstract: The effective resolution of non-deterministic polynomial time hard (NP-hard) combinatorial optimization problems requires a delicate balance between global exploration and local exploitation. While Quantum-Inspired Algorithms (QIAs) leverage principles of superposition to explore vast search spaces, they often lack the fine-grained exploitation capabilities of classical heuristics. To address this limitation, we propose the Quantum-Memetic Hybrid Algorithm (QMHA), a component-based framework that synergistically integrates qubit-based global search with adaptive classical refinement. The QMHA architecture explicitly coordinates five distinct algorithmic components: (1) quantum rotation gates for exploration, (2) a problem-aware memetic operator for immediate solution refinement, (3) an adaptive learning rate schedule, (4) periodic local search, and (5) a stagnation-based population reset for diversity management. We rigorously evaluate the framework against nine established metaheuristics, including Genetic Algorithms (GA), Differential Evolution (DE), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Simulated Annealing (SA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), MAX-MIN Ant System (MMAS), Memetic Algorithms (MA), Quantum Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA), and Harmony Search (HS), across a comprehensive benchmark suite comprising six NP-hard problem families: constrained combinatorial (Knapsack), graph-based (Max-Cut), permutation-based (TSP), constraint satisfaction (Graph Coloring), bin optimization (Bin Packing), and scheduling (Flow Shop Scheduling), as well as real-world machine learning (Feature Selection) problems and the continuous Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) 2022 benchmark. Statistical analysis using Friedman tests and Nemenyi post hoc comparisons confirms that QMHA achieves a statistically significant performance advantage (p&lt;0.004) and superior average rank (1.5) compared to component baselines and state-of-the-art competitors. Comprehensive analyses include computational complexity profiling, parameter sensitivity mapping, scalability testing up to D=2000, noise robustness evaluation, variable correlation degradation analysis, a six-component ablation study, exploration&ndash;exploitation dynamics tracking, integration mechanism comparison across five architectures, and a multi-objective extension feasibility study. The proposed framework offers a robust, verified approach to hybrid optimization without relying on biological metaphors.

title: MIMO-Net: Multi-Input Multi-Output Deep Learning Network for Full 12-Lead ECG Reconstruction from a Single Lead
abstract: The standard 12-lead ECG is the gold-standard tool for cardiac diagnosis and monitoring; however, its multi-electrode configuration limits its use in prolonged monitoring and wearable devices. Existing portable ECG devices typically record only a single lead, reducing their diagnostic value. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes novel Multi-Input Multi-Output neural networks (MIMO-Nets) that reconstruct a standard 12-lead ECG from a single raw ECG lead without requiring any feature extraction techniques. Four deep learning architectures were investigated: MIMO-Conv-Net, MIMO-U-Net, Conv-Net, and U-Net. Each model was trained and evaluated using all 12 standard ECG leads with different length L as candidate inputs to determine the optimal single-lead acquisition strategy. Results show that Lead II with L = 256 consistently provides the highest reconstruction performance across all architectures, making it the most informative single-lead input. Using Lead II as input, MIMO-U-Net yielded the highest reconstruction accuracy on a processed clinical dataset (ST-Petersburg INCART), with an average correlation of 0.864 at L = 256, closely followed by U-Net (0.862). On raw, unprocessed recordings from the PTB-XL database, both models achieved lower but still competitive correlations (0.740 and 0.732, respectively). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of single-lead-to-12-lead ECG reconstruction and highlight the role of signal preprocessing in reconstruction fidelity, supporting the development of wearable ECG systems for continuous cardiac monitoring.

title: Privacy-Preserving Transformers for Time-Series Forecasting: A Survey and Two-Axis Taxonomy of Cryptographic, Differential-Privacy, and Feature-Path Methods
abstract: Transformer architectures, originally developed for language modeling, have been increasingly applied to time-series forecasting, but deploying them on sensitive data such as patient vital signs, financial records, or energy use raises privacy risks at two points: inference (the server sees raw inputs and outputs) and training (the model can memorize individual records). This survey organizes privacy-preserving methods for Transformer forecasting along a two-axis taxonomy: protection stage (inference, training, and data-level) and protection locus/mechanism (cryptographic wrapper, gradient, input, feature, output, or data path). For inference, we review secure multi-party computation (CrypTen through MPCFormer, SecFormer, Iron, BOLT, PUMA, BumbleBee, and CipherPrune) and homomorphic encryption (CKKS, THE-X, hybrid HE-MPC, and automated FHE compilation via Orion), focusing on how each handles the Transformer non-linearities (softmax, GELU, and LayerNorm). For training, we organize differential-privacy mechanisms by where noise enters the gradient path (DP-SGD, DP-FedAvg, DP-FTRL, PATE, and adaptive clipping), the input path, and the more recent feature path and analyze the privacy, utility, and dimensionality trade-offs. We further survey privacy in large language and foundation models, federated Transformers, time-series privacy attacks (membership inference, gradient inversion, and attribute inference), differentially private synthetic data, and applications in energy, health care, and finance, closing with open problems and future directions. Throughout, we show that the surveyed mechanisms provide non-comparable privacy guarantees and should be chosen by threat model instead of headline utility.

title: Role-Aware Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Urban Rail Transit Fault Management
abstract: Urban rail transit systems require reliable decision-support methods to assist operators in handling complex fault events. Although large language models provide strong reasoning and knowledge integration capabilities, their open-ended generation may produce responses that are difficult to align with operational procedures. To address this issue, we propose a role-aware agentic retrieval-augmented generation framework for transit fault management. The framework integrates keyword-based retrieval, role-aware multi-agent reasoning, and constrained action generation within a unified architecture. Operational procedures and historical cases retrieved from transit knowledge repositories provide evidence for agent reasoning, while constrained outputs ensure that generated instructions remain consistent with predefined operational actions. Experimental results on a real-world urban rail transit emergency exercise dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the semantic score from 0.893 to 0.965 and increases Role F1 score from 0.824 to 0.915 compared with an Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) baseline while maintaining comparable inference efficiency. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework for decision support in urban rail transit fault scenarios.

title: Federated Convolutional Transformer Network for Privacy-Preserving Photovoltaic Fault Detection in Distributed Solar Power Systems
abstract: Solar energy makes a considerable contribution to global power generation, necessitating photovoltaic (PV) fault detection to ensure high yields in solar power systems. In real-world solar installations, operational data are geographically dispersed, heterogeneous, and sensitive, which imposes privacy restrictions. Existing PV fault-detection techniques have relied on centralized training, requiring raw image data from multiple plants to be collected at a single server, which has led to privacy risks, bias from heterogeneous datasets, and scalability issues. To overcome these challenges, this research provides a novel FL-based PV fault-detection model called Federated Convolutional Transformer Network (Fed-CVTNet), which combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture within the FL framework. Initially, the raw images are pre-processed to enhance the input quality, and the Region of Interest (ROI) is identified via a pretrained YOLO model. Then, the proposed Fed-CVTNet facilitates networked learning among many geographically dispersed clients by only sharing model updates using federated averaging (FedAvg). The experimental findings illustrate that the proposed FL model shows substantial quality improvements compared to the customized CNN-ViT models trained on a dataset of 5600 images and the CNN-ViT models that lack federated aggregation. The highest accuracy achieved by the proposed technique is 98.99%; the proposed Fed-CVTNet has better sensitivity (98.15%) and specificity (99.21%), and much lower false positive and false negative rates than its centralized counterparts. The comparative analysis establishes that federated weight aggregation outperforms centralized baseline models by 2.3% and is effective in reducing the data privacy risk.

title: Randomized Trials of AI-Based Interventions for Oral Healthcare and Dental Education: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being incorporated into oral healthcare and dental education, yet the quality and effectiveness of randomized evidence supporting these interventions remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating AI-based interventions in oral healthcare and dental education. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and OpenGrey from database inception to 30 June 2026. Twenty-eight published RCTs involving 2306 participants and 26 registered unpublished RCTs were identified. Educational applications represented the largest category (53.6%), followed by diagnosis and clinical decision support, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. Across the included RCTs, AI-based interventions were more frequently associated with improvements in educational performance, diagnostic accuracy, treatment planning, clinical decision-making, and periodontal monitoring than conventional approaches, although findings were heterogeneous, several studies reported no significant differences, and a small number favored conventional methods. No serious adverse events were reported, but safety reporting was inconsistent. Most published RCTs presented some concerns regarding risk of bias (82.1%), primarily related to randomization, deviations from intended interventions, and selective reporting. APPRAISE-AI demonstrated predominantly moderate methodological quality (median score 44%), with recurrent weaknesses in robustness, reproducibility, and data quality. The identification of 26 registered RCTs without published results also suggests a potential risk of dissemination bias. These findings indicate that AI-based interventions show promise across multiple applications in oral healthcare and dental education, but improvements in trial methodology, reporting quality, and transparency are needed to strengthen the evidence base and support clinical implementation.

title: Adapting Whisper to Karakalpak: Full, Layer-Selective, and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Low-Resource Speech Recognition
abstract: Building dependable automatic speech recognition (ASR) for Karakalpak is hindered by the scarcity of transcribed speech. Whisper handles many languages well, but without adaptation its Karakalpak transcripts remain unreliable, largely because the language combines agglutinative morphology with a Latin alphabet containing letters absent from most other orthographies. Following recent Whisper fine-tuning protocols, we adapt Whisper Large-v2 on the authors&rsquo; openly released Karakalpak Speech Corpus and compare full fine-tuning, layer-selective fine-tuning, and lightweight modules (bottleneck adapters and low-rank adaptation, LoRA) in an otherwise frozen network. On a speaker-independent test set, full fine-tuning reduces the word error rate (WER) from 37.70% to 13.53% and the character error rate from 15.40% to 5.42%. Freezing the lower 13 encoder layers gives comparable accuracy (13.39% WER), and adapters in the upper encoder layers and the decoder reach 15.59% WER with only 5.9M trainable parameters. Substituted special letters remain the most frequent error type. Full fine-tuning raises WER on closely related Kazakh and Uzbek by 4.6 and 6.6 percentage points, whereas adapters and LoRA largely preserve multilingual accuracy. The results provide a reproducible reference point for Karakalpak ASR that may later serve applications in education, public administration, accessibility, and digital language preservation.

title: Data Transformation and Scaling Methods for Zero-Inflated Sparse Data Analysis
abstract: Zero-inflated sparse count data are common in text analytics, where keyword frequencies contain many zeros and highly skewed positive values. This study proposes a systematic model-specific framework that treats predictor transformation and scaling as explicit modeling factors and evaluates their effects across statistically different count and machine-learning models. Raw, log, square root, and binary transformations are combined with no scaling, standard scaling, and maximum-absolute scaling. The resulting pipelines are evaluated using ridge regression, random forest, negative binomial regression, zero-inflated negative binomial regression, and a two-part negative binomial model on extended reality patent keyword data with varying levels of sparsity. The results show that preprocessing effects differ substantially across model classes. Random Forest showed strong predictive performance under the full predictor setting and required little preprocessing, whereas continuous transformations provided modest improvements for Ridge and two-part NB models. Binary transformation with standard scaling substantially improves the predictive stability of negative binomial and zero-inflated negative binomial models by reducing extreme errors and convergence problems. These findings demonstrate that transformation and scaling should be selected jointly with the prediction model, response sparsity, and analytical objective rather than applied as universal preprocessing steps.

title: Are Learner Personas Warranted? A Fuzzy-Clustering Diagnostic of Level and Shape in Learning-Attitude Profiles
abstract: Designers may use learner personas to plan different content, feedback, or support for groups of students, but a clustering result alone does not establish that these groups represent distinct learner types. Whether such a categorical structure exists in the data deriving those personas is rarely tested. This paper therefore proposes an uncertainty-aware fuzzy learner-modeling framework in which fuzzy partitioning serves as a diagnostic instrument rather than as a means of generating learner types. The study applies the framework to six learning-attitude constructs measured in three undergraduate cohorts taking AI-supported courses at a Taiwanese university of technology (N = 107; 90 retained after response-quality screening). It estimates fuzzy c-means partitions for two to five clusters at the primary fuzzifier value m = 2.0, with the two- and three-cluster solutions re-estimated at m = 1.5 and m = 2.5 as sensitivity checks. The two-cluster solution is stable (adjusted Rand index = 0.891) and reasonably crisp, yet all centroids differ only in overall level. Elevation accounts for 71.0% of the standardized variance, clustering the shape component alone is uninformative, and the structural criterion consequently fails. The construct with the lowest within-person centered standardized score relates to cohort (Monte Carlo p = 0.009), but no statistically significant association with modal cluster membership is detected (Monte Carlo p = 0.240). These findings insufficiently support distinct configural learner personas in this sample, using this instrument and these six constructs. The paper contributes to debates on person-centered learner modeling by specifying a diagnostic sequence that examines profile shape before interpreting stable, concentrated fuzzy partitions as learner personas. The support-priority vector remains an exploratory description of within-person score contrasts; its instructional value has not been tested.

title: Toward Explainable AI for Acute Kidney Injury Prediction in the ICU: Transparent Development, Internal Validation, and Robustness Auditing of Machine Learning Models
abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critical care, yet predictive artificial intelligence studies often differ in outcome definitions, validation, calibration, and interpretability. We developed and internally validated machine learning models for newly observed serum-creatinine-defined AKI after a fixed 24 h ICU landmark and then audited how stable the selected model was to clinically important observation and timing choices. Methods: Using MIMIC-IV v3.1, we retained one first ICU stay per adult patient, required adequate pre-landmark creatinine observation, excluded coded end-stage kidney disease, documented dialysis before the landmark, and observed AKI by the landmark. The outcome was a new creatinine rise within the next 48 h using KDIGO-aligned creatinine change thresholds, with follow-up truncated at ICU exit, hospital discharge, or death. The ascertainable cohort (n = 15,231) was split 60%/15%/10%/15% into training, calibration, validation, and test sets. Logistic regression, random forests, and histogram gradient boosting were calibrated with a separate calibration set; thresholds were fixed on validation data to target at least 80% sensitivity. The test set was evaluated once. A later post hoc audit reused frozen test risks without retraining. Results: Histogram gradient boosting was selected by validation average precision. In 2286 test patients (664 events; 29.0%), AUROC was 0.726 (95% CI, 0.701&ndash;0.749), average precision 0.523 (0.478&ndash;0.565), and Brier score 0.179 (0.171&ndash;0.187). At the fixed threshold, sensitivity was 78.5%, specificity 52.2%, positive predictive value 40.2%, and false alerts 33.9 per 100 patients. Mean predicted risk was 0.290 versus an observed event fraction of 0.290; calibration intercept and slope were 0.023 and 1.022. The AUROC difference versus full logistic regression was +0.0197 (95% CI, 0.00235&ndash;0.03571). Frozen-model sensitivity analyses produced AUROCs from 0.697 to 0.733 in most observation and measurement subsets. However, 15,900 otherwise eligible patients had indeterminate outcomes and showed substantially shorter follow-up and fewer post-landmark creatinine measurements. Conclusions: The selected model showed moderate discrimination and close aggregate calibration under internal validation. Discrimination was similar across several post hoc subsets, although calibration and threshold-based performance changed under stricter observation rules. The main limitation was observation-dependent outcome ascertainment. This work supports transparent model auditing as part of trustworthy AI evaluation, but it does not provide external validation, patient-level explanation validation, or evidence of clinical benefit. Multicenter temporal validation and prospectively defined observation rules are needed before clinical use.

title: Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Japanese Voice Cloning to Dub Chinese Short Dramas: A Four-System Benchmark with Human Evaluation
abstract: Chinese short-form dramas (duanju) drive a growing demand for automated Japanese dubbing that preserves each character&rsquo;s voice. The decisive component is zero-shot cross-lingual voice cloning: synthesising Japanese speech from a short Chinese reference clip. We benchmark four neural text-to-speech systems&mdash;GPT-SoVITS v3, F5-TTS, CosyVoice2-0.5B, and the non-cloning commercial baseline EdgeTTS&mdash;on an annotated short-drama corpus (79 episodes, 3692 segments, 12 speakers) with native-speaker-verified Japanese references, combining automatic intelligibility (Whisper re-transcription) and speaker-embedding similarity with a blind listening study by five JLPT-N1 raters. Among cloning systems, only GPT-SoVITS attains usable intelligibility (character error rate 0.215, against 1.152 for F5-TTS and 4.603 for CosyVoice2), while EdgeTTS is most intelligible overall (0.030). Critically, the automatic and perceptual measures dissociate: F5-TTS scores marginally higher on embedding similarity (0.729 vs. 0.722), yet raters preferr GPT-SoVITS three to one. Naturalness shows no detectable gap between GPT-SoVITS and EdgeTTS (mean opinion score 3.08 versus 3.12, p=0.93), a null result at a resolution of about 0.6 points. In a single-speaker probe, speaker similarity rises from 0.64 to 0.71 as the reference lengthens from 3 to 10 s. Embedding similarity alone is therefore an unreliable proxy for perceived speaker identity.

title: X-SLR: A Hexagonal Architecture Framework for Reporting Systematic Literature Reviews
abstract: Systematic literature reviews are essential for synthesizing scientific evidence but remain complex and resource-intensive processes that demand significant time and human effort. To reduce bias, they are usually conducted collaboratively and according to established methodologies. However, the way in which the process is documented, including the steps taken and the tools used, often depends on the author&rsquo;s preferences or basic guidelines of traditional methodologies. This variability makes it difficult to interpret the procedure and results and limits reproducibility for other researchers. This work introduces the Hexagonal Systematic Literature Review (X-SLR) architecture as a framework designed to standardize the reporting of procedures and results in systematic literature reviews. The X-SLR is based on the ports and adapters model from software engineering, which separates the core logic of a system from the tools and platforms used to implement it. Applied to reviews, the model conceptualizes the research goals as a central core connected to six functional components (ports): search strategy, selection criteria, data extraction, quality assessment, analysis and synthesis, and reporting. Each port can be linked to various tools through adapters. The proposed framework provides a structured mechanism for documenting review procedures, tool integration, and methodological decisions. By explicitly documenting port contracts, adapter choices, and traceability links, X-SLR is intended to help researchers assess whether tool substitutions preserve methodological coherence. A conceptual proposal, representative tool configurations, and a demonstration scenario are presented to illustrate the framework. The framework was retrospectively evaluated by applying a 25-item reporting checklist to a previously published SLR. Two independent coders achieved 88.0% agreement (Cohen&rsquo;s &kappa;=0.82), and the resulting Documentation Coverage score was 0.48. A separate internal formative assessment with two systematic review practitioners provided preliminary evidence regarding the clarity, traceability, complementarity, and usefulness of the X-SLR representation. These results provide preliminary evidence supporting X-SLR as a reporting and traceability artifact, while prospective studies are required to assess its effects on review execution, efficiency, and substantive reproducibility.

title: A Dated Corpus and a Seven-Layer Benchmark for Kazakhstani Legal Question Answering
abstract: Legal question answering is usually evaluated as if the law were static. In Kazakhstan, it changed twice within one year: a new Constitution replaced the 1995 text on 1 July 2026, and a new Tax Code replaced its predecessor on 1 January 2026, both reusing article numbers for different norms. We release a dated corpus of 41 Kazakhstani acts parsed to article level in both official languages (12,235 Russian and 11,973 Kazakh articles) and a benchmark of 150 question-answer pairs in seven layers, two of which score declining to answer and asking for a date. Two practising lawyers confirmed every pair. Comparing a no-retrieval baseline, retrieval-augmented generation and a tool-using agent, we find that retrieval rather than generation accounts for most citation error, measured against each pair&rsquo;s source articles: given the gold article, the model cites it in 92% of cases, and retrieval alone reduces citations of non-existent norms from 31% to zero. The agent adds nothing on this measure and abstains far less often. Dense retrieval improves citation recall but nearly doubles the repealed norms presented as current; date-aware ranking removes them for every retriever, although under dense retrieval it also removes three historically required citations. The retrieval findings are reproduced on two open models.

title: Structured Knowledge Extraction from Wheat Variety Approval Texts via Relation-Aware In-Context Learning and Progressive Knowledge Calibration
abstract: Knowledge extraction serves as a critical technique for constructing domain-specific knowledge graphs and enabling intelligent text parsing. In the vertical agricultural domain, wheat variety approval texts contain abundant agronomic trait entities and their relational associations. Nevertheless, they are characterized by dense domain-specific terminology, the co-occurrence of multiple relations, long entity spans, and mixed numerical and textual expressions, which pose considerable challenges to the accurate extraction of entity-relation triples. Existing in-context learning paradigms mostly retrieve demonstrations based on general-purpose semantic embeddings. The retrieved demonstrations rarely achieve relation-structure matching with query instances; furthermore, LLMs are susceptible to format hallucinations, which limit entity and relation extraction performance. Accordingly, we propose Relation-aware Demonstration Retrieval and Progressive Knowledge Calibration for In-Context Learning (ReCal-ICL), a relation-aware in-context learning framework for joint entity and relation extraction. ReCal-ICL employs RADS, a relation-aware demonstration selector based on hierarchical contrastive learning. Through hierarchical quadruples, in-batch dynamic negative sampling, and a hybrid loss, RADS reshapes the representation space to enhance relational-structure matching between retrieved demonstrations and query instances. In addition, a two-layer output constraint strategy is developed, which integrates prompt-template prior constraints and post hoc result verification mechanisms to jointly guarantee the format compliance of extraction outputs. We conduct comparative and ablation experiments on WVAD as well as public NYT and CoNLL04 datasets. Experimental results show that ReCal-ICL achieves competitive joint extraction performance across multiple datasets. Further experiments show that incorporating demonstrations benefits downstream extraction, while the retrieval relevance evaluation indicates that RADS improves the relational relevance of retrieved demonstrations.

title: A Textile Standardization Large Language Model Integrating LoRA Fine-Tuning and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Intelligent question answering for textile standards requires accurate domain understanding, clause retrieval, and evidence-grounded generation, yet general-purpose large language models often lack sufficient domain adaptation and factual support. This study proposes a textile-standard question-answering framework that integrates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning with multidimensional retrieval-augmented generation (MDRAG). Based on 7017 domestic and international textile standards, we constructed a structured knowledge resource containing 121,166 annotated domain elements and a task-specific dataset of 2000 question&ndash;answer pairs. Qwen3.5-9B-Base, Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct, and GLM-4-9B were evaluated under three primary settings: Baseline, Baseline+LoRA, and Baseline+LoRA+MDRAG. A separate comparison with conventional RAG was conducted to assess the additional benefit of multidimensional retrieval over single-path retrieval. Among the primary settings, Qwen3.5-9B-Base with LoRA+MDRAG achieved the highest overall performance, with a cosine similarity of 0.624, a BLEU score of 0.283, and an expert-based overall score of 24.4. These findings support the use of lightweight domain adaptation together with multidimensional structured knowledge retrieval for textile-standard question answering.

title: Team Cognition Under Algorithmic Management: Evidence from Distributed Software Development Teams
abstract: Algorithmic systems increasingly shape how distributed software teams monitor work and evaluate performance, but their relationship with shared team understanding remains unclear. This study examined perceived algorithmic monitoring and evaluation (AME), supportive leadership, team mental models, and technical task-output performance in 72 distributed software development teams from 32 firms participating in Horizon Europe projects. Survey responses from 317 team members were averaged to team scores and matched with five GTmetrix indicators of each team&rsquo;s delivered output collected six months later. Averaged perceptions of AME and of supportive leadership were each positively associated with averaged perceived shared understanding. These associations held when the nesting of teams within firms was modeled, but between-team reliability of the aggregated measures was low (ICC(2) &le; 0.16), so they are associations among team-averaged perceptions rather than evidence of reliable differences in shared team cognition. AME showed nominal associations with two highly correlated technical indicators that did not survive adjustment for multiple testing and were weaker in a web-only subsample of 59 teams that excluded mobile applications measured through store listing pages; the indicators describe page performance under observed deployment conditions. No statistically detectable moderation by supportive leadership was found, and the exploratory, firm-unadjusted bootstrap gave no evidence of a conditional indirect association through team mental models. The study locates the empirical boundaries of a team-cognition account of algorithmic management: perceptual associations are present, but the proposed path to technical performance is not supported in these data.

title: Structure-Guided Texture Enhancement and Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for Progressive Mural Inpainting
abstract: Progressive mural inpainting requires structural guidance to reconstruct missing textures while maintaining color consistency. Existing methods only introduce line constraints at the input stage, resulting in distorted structures and color mismatch for severely damaged murals. This paper proposes SGMA-MuralNet, a two-stage network integrating structure-conditioned deep feature modulation and multi-scale feature aggregation (MFA). A full-line encoder applies affine modulation on channel-local normalized features in middle encoder layers to retain fine mural structures. The MFA module uses parallel dilated convolutions and channel recalibration to capture multi-range context. A color correction network (CCN) predicts signed residual for color alignment, and mask compositing keeps intact original pixels. Evaluated on DhMurals1714 with 10&ndash;60% irregular damage masks, our model reaches 28.65 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), 0.926 structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and 0.034 learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS), outperforming MuralNet with +1.37 dB PSNR and 30.6% LPIPS reduction. Visual results verify its capability to restore facial contours and flowing ribbons with coherent color transitions. The contribution is an incremental architectural integration of established structural conditioning and multi-scale aggregation mechanisms within MuralNet&rsquo;s progressive structure reconstruction network (SRN)&ndash;CCN framework. The reported results support its utility for benchmark mural inpainting conditioned on supplied registered drawings; they do not establish the historical authenticity of generated details.

title: Semantic Federated Clustering for Cross-Domain Recommendation with Interaction Graphs
abstract: In federated cross-domain recommendation, the existing research has widely focused on scenarios where at least some users or items overlap. How to enable cross-domain recommendation over non-overlapping users and items has emerged as a challenging research direction. However, current privacy-preserving cross-domain recommendation methods struggle to achieve effective semantic alignment across domains in such scenarios, hindering their ability to capture latent correlations between interaction graphs. Moreover, when refining noisy node representations and interaction sequences, these methods often overlook temporal noise implicitly embedded in semantic information, as well as the potential of jointly leveraging textual and temporal features for collaborative denoising. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Semantic Federated Clustering-driven Cross-Domain Recommendation model (SFC-CDR). Specifically, we first design a clustering-anchored contrastive learning framework that performs clustering using weighted multi-layer node semantic representations. The weighted aggregated centroids serve as semantic anchors to dynamically update the pool of positive and negative samples in contrastive learning, thereby achieving geometric alignment in the shallow feature space and capturing fine-grained semantic correlations in the implicit concept space. Furthermore, we design a Joint Temporal&ndash;Frequency Filtering (JTFF) module. In the frequency domain, features are processed via an MoE adapter and FFT-based filtering, while in the temporal domain, a temporal convolutional network (TCN) is employed to model temporal patterns in user&ndash;item interaction sequences. The resulting temporal and frequency-domain representations are integrated through Temporal&ndash;Frequency Refinement Gating (TFRG), enabling complementary refinement of node semantic representations and user behavior sequences. Extensive experiments conducted on four real-world datasets demonstrate that SFC-CDR outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Disciplinary Cultures and the Diffusion of Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Bibliometric Study of Music and Acoustics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in scientific research and artistic practice, yet its publication patterns vary across research contexts. This study presents a comparative bibliometric analysis of 655 publications retrieved from five databases. We examine publication trends, authorship patterns, national contributions, application areas, and the reported use of AI model families across three analytical categories: STEM&ndash;Sound-only (SSO), STEM&ndash;Music-explicit (SME), and Music-Focused AI (MFAI), where STEM denotes science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. The corpus comprises 139 SSO, 496 SME, and 20 MFAI publications. Publication output increased markedly after 2018, particularly in SSO and SME. Within the retrieved corpus, recurrent neural networks, convolutional neural networks, and Transformers appeared earlier in SME than in SSO, whereas MFAI included earlier work applying machine learning to sound design. Sole-authored papers accounted for 60% of MFAI publications, compared with 15.5% in SME and 2.2% in SSO. China had the largest publication count in SSO and SME, while no contributions from Chinese institutional affiliations were identified in the MFAI sample. These findings document differences in research output, collaboration patterns, geographical participation, and the timing of reported model use across publication contexts. They provide an empirical basis for further investigation of interdisciplinary exchange.

title: Greedy and Stepwise Feature Selection for Network Intrusion Detection: A Systematic Review and Decision Workflow
abstract: Feature selection is widely used in machine-learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs/NIDSs) to reduce dimensionality and computational burden, yet its benefits are difficult to attribute when feature evaluation, subset search, preprocessing, classifier design, and deployment conditions are assessed together. This systematic review analyzed 104 IDS/NIDS studies published from 2010 to 2026, identified through Scopus and Web of Science and supplemented by targeted Google Scholar searches. The corpus comprised 56 filter/relevance, 18 greedy/sequential, 28 hybrid/metaheuristic contrast, and 2 Other/Unclear studies. We assessed feature reduction, computational reporting, repeated-run evidence, feature-subset stability, leakage control, online cost, and deployment evidence. Among 42 studies with a single unambiguous reduction value, the median feature reduction was 73.8% (IQR: 59.3&ndash;84.2%). The runtime or computational cost was reported in 56.7% of studies and independent repeated runs in 9.6%, and no study explicitly evaluated feature-subset stability. Leakage-safe processing was clearly demonstrated in 13.5%, whereas 56.7% presented potential leakage risk; clear or partial deployment evidence was available in 6.7%. Out of six strict same-study comparisons, broader hybrid/metaheuristic methods improved reported detection performance in five, but gains in feature reduction and computational cost were inconsistent. Based on these findings, the review formulates feature-selection choice as a resource-constrained decision problem and proposes an algorithmic conditional-escalation workflow in which a broader search is introduced only when simpler strategies fail to satisfy predefined predictive or operational constraints. Additional search complexity should therefore be justified by comparable, reproducible, leakage-safe, and deployment-relevant evidence rather than by cross-study accuracy alone.

title: Multi-Level Transformations Induced by GenAI in Instructional Design: A Thematic Analysis of a Reddit Forum
abstract: Research on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) integration into instructional design practice has been expanding rapidly; however, its effects on the instructional design profession remain underexplored. To this end, this study examines instructional designers&rsquo; perceptions about how GenAI is reshaping the instructional design professional landscape and how online communities engage them in sharing those perceptions. Using a mixed-methods data analysis method including automatic text mining and human verification, a large data set obtained from an online community of instructional designers on Reddit was analyzed thematically. Results revealed three key changes at professional, organizational, and individual levels, and the mechanisms shaping instructional designers&rsquo; engagement in their online community. Namely, GenAI has already started to reshape the instructional design landscape through a mixed set of changes including transformations, adaptations and reconfigurations, and an online community can function as an informal community of practice for instructional designers to collectively share experiential wisdom and necessary competencies to successfully navigate the emergent transitions. This study contributes by uncovering the changes happening in instructional design due to GenAI and how informal online channels can work as communities of practice that are distributed, asynchronous, on-demand knowledge exchange avenues, thus increasing instructional designers&rsquo; awareness and collective preparedness.

title: A Leakage-Aware Evaluation Framework and Benchmark for Edge-Based Multi-Sensor Fire and Smoke Detection
abstract: Low-cost multi-sensor nodes are increasingly used to detect fire and smoke inside buildings, where separating flame from smouldering emission determines the response. Such detectors are usually validated on densely sampled logs whose consecutive readings are nearly identical. Earlier studies report near-perfect accuracy in this setting but seldom state whether the train&ndash;test split respected event boundaries; when it does not, the score measures memorisation rather than generalisation. This paper treats the evaluation itself as the object of study. A controlled single-room testbed with temperature, humidity, gas, and particulate sensing produced a labelled time-series dataset with exactly known event boundaries, so that leakage could be introduced or excluded deliberately. Six methods were evaluated on identical data under a random split and under an event-preserving split using the macro-averaged F1 score, which weights minority classes equally. The random split yielded markedly higher three-class scores for every supervised model, whereas hazard-versus-normal detection was largely unaffected. Holding out single events revealed strong between-event variability, while thinning records within events changed results only slightly: independent events, not records, are the binding constraint. The dataset, code, and a short leakage-aware protocol are released; the findings characterise the evaluation protocol under controlled conditions, not field performance.

title: An Integrated ETL&ndash;OLAP and Semantic Retrieval Architecture for Hybrid Analysis of Structured and Unstructured Enterprise Data
abstract: Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) and Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) provide robust mechanisms for integrating structured data and supporting multidimensional analysis. Still, they offer limited support for semantic access to unstructured textual content. This study proposes an integrated architecture that combines conventional ETL and data warehousing with semantic retrieval based on dense vector representations and similarity search. The architecture separates structured analytical processing from semantic document retrieval while preserving traceability among source documents, warehouse records, and vector representations. The architecture was examined through an implementation-oriented case study using a large document collection of up to 1.58 million PDF files. The study reports descriptive implementation observations on data ingestion, vector indexing, and query execution in the deployed environment. These observations characterize the operational behavior of the implemented system and are not presented as a controlled performance benchmark between OLAP and semantic retrieval, because the two mechanisms address different classes of information needs. The architecture also provides a query-time foundation for downstream Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG); however, this study does not assess generative response quality or LLM orchestration as case-study outcomes. Accordingly, this work contributes primarily through the architectural integration of structured analytical processing and semantic retrieval, preservation of document-to-warehouse-to-vector traceability, and practical implementation of the framework over a large enterprise document repository. The study also identifies limitations related to repeated timing measurements, stage-level profiling, independently annotated relevance judgments, and retrieval-effectiveness assessment. These limitations define future work involving Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG, controlled workload benchmarking, and systematic evaluation of RAG-generated responses.

title: DyGRAV: Dynamic Grounding and Relational Reasoning for Vision&ndash;Language Navigation
abstract: Vision&ndash;Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to interpret natural-language instructions in 3D environments. While significant progress has been made, state-of-the-art agents often struggle with instructions that demand fine-grained visual understanding, correctly grounding specific object attributes, distinguishing between similar objects, and interpreting complex spatial relationships. Many methods rely on static visual features or on global cross-modal attention and lack mechanisms to dynamically resolve ambiguities during navigation. We propose DyGRAV (Dynamic Grounding and Relational Reasoning for VLN), which is a dynamic, uncertainty-aware framework that augments a strong VLN backbone with two adaptively triggered reasoning modules. The Contextual VLM Querying module detects grounding ambiguity for descriptive phrases (e.g., &ldquo;the ceramic bowl&rdquo;) and issues targeted queries to a vision&ndash;language model (e.g., CLIP) using current visual evidence, while the Incremental Relational Scene Graph (IRSG) constructs lightweight, task-relevant relational memory online to resolve complex spatial relations (e.g., &ldquo;the chair next to the window&rdquo;). A budget-aware gating mechanism regulates when these modules are invoked, optimizing the balance between reasoning quality and computational cost through value-per-cost selection and hard budget constraints. Comprehensive evaluations on R2R and RxR, along with a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark emphasizing attribute and relation understanding, show that DyGRAV achieves superior navigation accuracy on challenging instructions while maintaining bounded per-step compute budgets with 97.33% episode-level adherence.

title: LAB@SMART: A Digital Workflow for Continuous Formative Assessment in FPGA-Based Digital Systems Laboratories
abstract: The digital transformation of engineering education has created new opportunities to support laboratory learning through continuous formative assessment. However, digital technologies are frequently implemented as isolated tools rather than as components of a coherent pedagogical framework. This paper presents LAB@SMART, an integrated digital framework that supports the complete FPGA-based laboratory learning cycle by combining pre-laboratory preparation, in-class formative assessment, laboratory practice, post-laboratory consolidation, and continuous feedback within a unified workflow. The framework integrates complementary digital technologies with conventional laboratory teaching without requiring modifications to the curriculum or laboratory infrastructure. A pilot deployment was conducted during the second semester of the 2025/2026 academic year in a Digital Systems Laboratory course involving two laboratory groups (35 students). The evaluation combined academic performance, informal implementation observations, and an anonymous student questionnaire. Among students who attended the examinations, the pilot groups showed a slightly higher pass rate than the remaining course cohort while also obtaining a slightly higher average final grade. Students also reported positive perceptions of the integrated workflow, particularly regarding laboratory preparation, continuous monitoring of their learning progress, and formative feedback. Although the pilot was limited in duration and scale, the results provide preliminary evidence of the practical feasibility of the proposed framework and support its further evaluation in other engineering laboratory contexts.

title: The Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Self-Regulated Learning: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: This meta-analysis systematically examined the effects of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on students&rsquo; self-regulated learning (SRL), including its overall effectiveness and its impact on the cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioral dimensions of SRL. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this study conducted a random-effects meta-analysis to synthesize evidence from 17 studies. The results revealed a statistically significant positive average effect of GenAI on SRL (Hedges&rsquo; g = 0.74). Nevertheless, substantial between-study heterogeneity suggested considerable variation in the magnitude of this effect across educational contexts. Positive average effects were also observed across the cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioral dimensions of SRL. However, a multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with CR2-robust inference indicated that effect sizes did not differ significantly across these dimensions (p = 0.564). Moderator analyses revealed significant differences in effect sizes associated with experimental design and intervention duration, whereas no significant differences were observed for subject domain, GenAI intervention type, GenAI tool, or personalization. Overall, the findings suggest that GenAI has the potential to contribute to the development of SRL, highlighting the importance of using GenAI as a scaffold to support, rather than replace, learners&rsquo; active self-regulatory processes.

title: Event Log Behavioral Privacy Protection Method Based on Relaxed Behavioral Profiles
abstract: Privacy preservation techniques for event logs prevent sensitive information leakage by injecting noise into log data, thus mitigating privacy risks in business process management. While ensuring privacy, this approach often reduces data utility and impacts subsequent analysis accuracy. Current research mainly optimizes noise injection based on data attributes to preserve utility, but overlooks how behavioral relationship changes affect data quality. To address this, this paper proposes a privacy protection method for event logs based on relaxed behavioral profiles. First, a behavioral privacy attack model is formalized to reveal how behavioral relationships can lead to privacy leakage. Building on this, data attributes are utilized to extend behavioral profiles, and a behavioral profile extension algorithm is proposed to analyze implicit behavioral relationships between activities. This allows building a multi-perspective perturbation set combining behavioral and data attributes. Finally, perturbations are injected using differential privacy methods. Experiments on both real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that the event logs generated by this method are behavior-unchanged at the level of the modeled relations, effectively mitigating the utility loss caused by log anonymization and attaining F1-scores of up to 0.874 on synthetic data, comparable to those of the baselines.

title: Shipping in 76 Locales: A Multi-Case Study of LLM-Agent Localization Pipelines for Production Mobile Apps
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents translate software interfaces at scale, yet production evidence on what breaks&mdash;and which safeguards catch it&mdash;is nearly absent: a 2026 mapping study of localization testing retained 24 primary studies, though none on LLM-driven localization. We report a multi-case study of fourteen shipped mobile apps by one developer (ten iOS, four Android; 40&ndash;76 locales; roughly 347,000 units) at five maturity levels. Mining the repositories (catalogs, 4473 commits, process documents, tooling), we code defects into thirteen classes in two waves, the second under a frozen codebook, and map each to its detecting layer. Translation quality is not independently measured; the defect record is a lower bound. Of 468 commit-anchored defects, process and coverage gaps&mdash;strings escaping the pipeline&mdash;are modal in each wave (26.7% and 27.5%); placeholder errors are near-absent (9 in 347,000 units). LLM judges are the largest operational detector (26.7%), ahead of humans (16.0%) and validators (13.7%), yet 127 defects (27.1%) escaped every layer until our audit. What escapes tracks validator scope, not maturity alone. Layered validation, not prompt-level care, determines what reaches users. Translation takes minutes; the validation stack is the lasting cost. We derive six testable propositions and ten guidelines, and release the codebook, dataset, and scripts.

title: SparseRoute: Structured Sparse Variable Routing for High-Dimensional Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Forecasting high-dimensional multivariate time series requires models to represent dependencies across variables without making variable interactions prohibitively expensive. Full attention over variable-level tokens has a pairwise cost quadratic in the number of variables; channel-independent methods avoid this cost but omit explicit cross-variable interactions. SparseRoute addresses this design choice by assigning variables to a small set of learned subspaces and applying attention to their aggregated representations. A vector-quantization routing module produces hard variable-to-subspace assignments, while a straight-through estimator supplies surrogate gradients during training. A dual-path decoder combines subspace predictions broadcast to their assigned variables with variable-level predictions from a shared multilayer perceptron. We evaluate the model with three seeds on Traffic, Electricity, Solar-Energy, PEMS04, and PEMS07. SparseRoute obtains the lowest mean MAE for Traffic at horizon 96 and the lowest mean MSE at horizon 192; Crossformer leads on several other dataset&ndash;horizon pairs. Relative to a dense variable-token model with matched tokenization and backbone, routing changes the pairwise attention factor from the square of the variable count to the square of the subspace count; this theoretical comparison does not establish an end-to-end resource advantage over the external baselines.

title: A Mobile-Centric Approach to Improving the Performance of Decentralized Wireless Networks
abstract: The proliferation of wireless devices and intelligent environments has led to increasingly dense, interference-prone Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) deployments. Recent amendments, such as IEEE 802.11ax/be, aim to enhance spatial reuse (SR) by optimizing spectrum efficiency. However, current SR initiatives face significant deployment challenges, including incompatibility with legacy 802.11 versions, a lack of centralized coordination, the difficulty for Access Points (APs) to monitor their neighborhood while maintaining uninterrupted service, and limited monitoring range. We argue that these limitations stem from the traditional AP-centric approach. In contrast, this work proposes a mobile-centric SR approach that overcomes these issues. Our method uses roaming mobile terminals (MTs) to independently monitor neighboring AP parameters (channel, transmission power, carrier-sense threshold), regardless of the 802.11 version or owner. After collecting local topological information, MTs execute a two-stage optimization: first, a local channel selection heuristic, followed by an algorithm that uses a pre-trained neural network to quickly evaluate and select the best transmission power and carrier-sense threshold for each in-range AP. MTs then broadcast these recommended parameters opportunistically using unassociated management frames, allowing them to be modified on the fly. By using a pre-trained model, our system does not need to learn in real time; consequently, network convergence is primarily governed by how quickly the mobile terminals explore and cover the deployment area, which depends on factors such as terminal speed, number of mobile terminals, trajectory characteristics, and pause times. Simulation results demonstrate that this mobile-centric approach quickly identifies near-optimal AP configurations, achieving throughput performance comparable to the reinforcement learning approaches considered in this study while exhibiting substantially shorter estimate

title: A Conversational AI Framework for Teacher Training
abstract: This paper introduces ETQ-AI (Effective Teaching Questionnaire&mdash;Artificial Intelligence), a conversational AI framework designed to support teacher professional development by identifying pedagogical misconceptions and fostering critical reflection. Building on Evidence-Informed Education (EIE) principles, the system integrates a 50-item diagnostic questionnaire with an automated, Gemini-driven Explainable AI (XAI) feedback layer. When teachers complete the diagnostic form, they receive personalized feedback and can engage in dialogic interactions with Google Gemini to explore the underlying meta-analytic evidence (e.g., Hattie&rsquo;s effect sizes, Cognitive Load Theory) or argue personal objections. We evaluated system fidelity against an expert panel benchmark (N=64 items) and conducted a pilot evaluation with 123 educators (70 primary teachers, 40 secondary teachers, 13 school leaders) recruited at an EIE conference. Gemini demonstrated high alignment with expert evaluations (97%), matching or exceeding static baseline feedback in user satisfaction (Mean = 4.1/5 vs. 3.8/5). Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 participant objections revealed key areas of tension, particularly around contextual constraints and pedagogical subjectivity. While the findings validate the technical proof-of-concept, system usability, and user engagement of ETQ-AI as an interactive scaffolding interface, we emphasize that this pilot study measures user perceptions and conversational patterns rather than direct pre/post shifts in critical reflection or classroom instructional practice.

title: Quality-by-Design Framework for Evaluating AI-Driven Machine Translation in Regulatory Affairs
abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine translation increasingly prepares multilingual product information for EU marketing authorisation, yet no established process exists to adapt or validate a system for the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC), whose sections differ in regulatory function, terminology, and clinical risk. This work develops such a process and a qualification procedure against the approved human translation. Methods: An EMA-derived ontology divides the SmPC into seven regulatory domains, each with a provisional ICH Q9 risk profile, following Quality-by-Design principles. A No Language Left Behind model was fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation on an eight-language-pair corpus and compared with the pre-trained model using BLEU, chrF, TER and COMET. Quality was validated by a five-layer, human-sign-off pipeline. Results: Fine-tuning improved every metric for every language pair. Quality varied more by domain than by language, hidden by corpus-level scores, and the domains rated highest-risk, under provisional ratings awaiting external calibration, were not the best translated. Checks on language-independent quantities were reliable everywhere; within adverse-reaction sections, the terminology check was the only partial-anchor instrument, and it showed meaningful gains only after a second language-model stage. Conclusions: The fine-tuned model and its validation pipeline, targeting automated checks where reliable and human review elsewhere, form a promising assistive step under qualified sign-off whose suitability for production-scale deployment requires further validation; assessment must be by regulatory domain, not the document as a whole.

title: How Do Different Components Affect Story Illustration? From Narrative Processing to Prompt Repair
abstract: Illustrated stories support children&rsquo;s learning. They also aid digital publishing and preserve regional narratives. However, manual illustration is costly and difficult to scale. Diffusion models offer an alternative. Yet, they often omit narrative details. They may also alter recurring characters across scenes. This work tries to find answers to three research questions concerning diffusion-based story visualization. First, we study how scene segmentation and part-of-speech filtering influence narrative alignment. Second, we evaluate IP-Adapter and consistent self-attention for cross-scene identity preservation and examine their trade-offs with scene diversity and narrative fidelity. Finally, we propose an attention-guided prompt-repair method that measures the grounding of required entities, attributes, relations, and character states and then iteratively revises prompts. Our experiments indicate that image conditioning improves character continuity but can restrict scene variation. The proposed framework converts diffusion attention from a post hoc explanation into an automatic signal for diagnosing and repairing story prompts.

title: Benchmarking Local Large Language Models for Structured Knowledge Extraction in Conversational Commerce
abstract: The integration of natural language understanding into conversational commerce requires robustly extracting structured intents from idiomatic text. While cloud-based models are highly capable, their latency, privacy risks, and operational costs necessitate efficient local alternatives. To address this, we empirically evaluate locally deployed, open-weights Large Language Models (LLMs) on parsing multi-intent shopping cart commands into deterministic JSON schemas. We benchmark multiple models across minimal, extended, and few-shot prompting paradigms, utilizing a dual-axis framework to simultaneously measure extraction quality (operation F1-score, exact match, schema validity) and hardware performance (latency, GPU power consumption). Our evaluation highlights a fundamental trade-off between schema compliance and computational overhead, demonstrating how advanced prompting techniques improve parsing accuracy while measurably impacting inference latency and power draw. Ultimately, this comprehensive profiling identifies optimal model configurations for resource-constrained environments: a well-chosen 3-8B parameter model (specifically Granite4 3B) paired with few-shot prompting recovers over 95% of the quality of the largest evaluated model at a coarse indicative estimate of 40&times; lower operational energy per command, establishing a practical baseline for deploying cost-effective LLMs as efficiency candidates in resource-constrained environments.

title: BAP-YOLO: A Pear Disease and Pest Detection Algorithm for Natural Orchard Environments
abstract: Pest and disease detection in natural pear orchard environments is often affected by branch and leaf occlusion, non-uniform illumination, and complex background textures. In addition, substantial variations exist in the morphology and scale of lesions and insect-damaged regions, while the weak texture features of early-stage lesions can be progressively attenuated during feature propagation. Therefore, effectively representing targets at different scales while preserving discriminative local details and suppressing irrelevant background information is crucial for improving pest and disease detection in pear orchards. To address these challenges, this study proposes BAP-YOLO, a detection framework designed for natural pear orchard environments. The framework progressively enhances feature representation through context aggregation, adaptive scale modeling, and discriminative detail refinement. First, a Branch-based Target Enhancement Fusion (BTEF) module is introduced into the backbone network to enhance hierarchical feature representations at multiple backbone stages, thereby reducing interference from complex background information in target representation. Second, an Adaptive Scale Dynamic (ASD) module is designed and embedded into the neck network to construct candidate features with different effective receptive fields and dynamically modulate their contributions using multi-resolution statistics, thereby improving the model&rsquo;s ability to detect targets with substantial scale variations.
