Analisis Komparatif Kinerja Algoritma Naive Bayes dengan dan tanpa Seleksi Fitur Chi-Square untuk Deteksi Spam Email
abstract: <jats:p>Email telah menjadi alat komunikasi vital, namun efektivitasnya terdegradasi oleh volume spam yang tinggi. Algoritma Naive Bayes (NB) adalah metode machine learning yang populer untuk klasifikasi spam. Namun, kinerja NB dapat dipengaruhi oleh tingginya dimensi data (jumlah fitur kata yang sangat banyak). Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dampak seleksi fitur Chi-Square  terhadap kinerja Naive Bayes. Metode penelitian ini adalah analisis komparatif antara dua model: (A) Naive Bayes standar, dan (B) Naive Bayes dengan seleksi fitur Chi-Square. Kedua model menggunakan vektorisasi TF-IDF pada dataset Enron yang berisi 33.716 email. Model A menggunakan 5.000 fitur, sedangkan Model B direduksi menjadi 1.000 fitur terbaik hasil seleksi . Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Model A (tanpa ) telah mencapai akurasi sangat tinggi sebesar 98,1%. Model B (dengan ) mampu mencapai akurasi yang hampir identik sebesar 98,0%, dengan nilai presisi dan recall yang juga serupa. Kesimpulan dari penelitian ini adalah penerapan Chi-Square pada kasus ini tidak meningkatkan akurasi (karena model dasar sudah mencapai kinerja puncak), namun terbukti sangat efektif dalam mereduksi dimensi fitur sebesar 80% (dari 5.000 menjadi 1.000 fitur) sambil tetap mempertahankan kinerja model. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi NB+ menghasilkan model yang jauh lebih efisien secara komputasi.</jats:p>

title: PCLA-Bridge: The Reusability of CARLA-Trained Autonomous Driving Agents beyond the CARLA Simulator
AI Coding Agents on GitHub: Repository Popularity as a Hidden Confounder in the Acceptance of 2.4 Million Agent-Authored Pull Requests
abstract:
<jats:p>Autonomous coding agents now open pull requests on GitHub without a person writing the code, and the share of
those pull requests that maintainers merge has become the usual shorthand for how well the agents work. This paper argues that
the shorthand measures the projects as much as it measures the agents. Using the public AIDev dataset, a snapshot of 2,743,854
pull requests written by six agents across 326,798 repositories between December 2024 and October 2025, we find that the merge
rate falls from 91.58 percent in repositories with no stars to 60.05 percent in repositories with a thousand or more. The decline
appears inside every agent separately, and in the five agents with enough volume in the top band to measure it the fall is between
20.3 and 27.6 percentage points, so it cannot be an artefact of which agent is used where. The enriched portion of the dataset
that previously published analyses rely on contains only repositories with at least 100 stars, which we verify directly; it holds 2.7
percent of the decided pull requests and merges them at 73.67 percent against 90.63 percent elsewhere. Holding the repository
fixed with a Mantel-Haenszel estimator changes the picture between agents: of fifteen comparable pairs, two reverse direction
and one loses more than half its effect.
Time to a decision separates the same way, a median of 51 seconds in unstarred repositories against 5.4 hours in the most
popular ones, with a medium effect size. Even within the enriched subset, 75.8 percent of agent pull requests carry no recorded
human review. We conclude that published acceptance figures describe a narrow and unusually demanding slice of GitHub, and
we recommend that studies of agent contributions report the popularity distribution of their repositories and estimate effects
within repositories rather than across them.</jats:p>

title: Penerapan Random Forest untuk Identifikasi Tipe Kepribadian: Studi Kasus Klasifikasi Introvert dan Extrovert
abstract: <jats:p>Pengelompokan tipe kepribadian menjadi salah satu cara penting untuk memahami bagaimana individu berinteraksi dalam konteks sosial. Penelitian ini mengeksplorasi penerapan algoritma pembelajaran mesin dalam membedakan individu ke dalam dua kategori kepribadian utama: introvert dan ekstrovert, berdasarkan indikator perilaku sosial yang dapat diukur secara kuantitatif. Dataset yang digunakan mencakup 2.900 observasi dengan variabel-variabel seperti durasi waktu yang diluangkan secara mandiri, frekuensi partisipasi dalam kegiatan sosial, tingkat interaksi di luar lingkungan rumah, serta jumlah teman dalam jaringan sosial. Sebelum analisis, data mengalami proses pra-pemrosesan yang meliputi konversi variabel kategorikal menjadi bentuk numerik dan penskalaan fitur numerik agar seragam. Model klasifikasi yang digunakan adalah Random Forest Classifier dengan parameter baku, yang divalidasi menggunakan pembagian data latih dan uji melalui teknik stratified split untuk menjaga keseimbangan distribusi kelas. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan performa model yang baik, dengan tingkat akurasi sebesar 90,86% dan F1-Score mencapai 91,03%. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa pendekatan berbasis pembelajaran mesin, terutama model ensemble seperti Random Forest memiliki potensi besar dalam mengidentifikasi ciri kepribadian melalui pola perilaku sosial yang terekam.</jats:p>

title: LLM Agents Can See Code Repositories
REAP: Automatic Curation of Coding Agent Benchmarks from Interactive Production Usage
Disclosure Failure in Compromised AI Coding Agents
abstract:
<jats:p>Software developers increasingly delegate routine programming work to autonomous AI coding agents that read untrusted project files, run commands, and call external services with limited human review. No developer can audit every action such an agent takes, so oversight defaults to a single artifact: the summary the agent writes when it finishes. The completeness of that summary is a security property in its own right, yet current evaluations do not measure it. Existing benchmarks ask whether a malicious instruction planted in a repository succeeds in redirecting an agent. They do not ask whether the agent then discloses what it did.
This study takes up the second question. We instrument an open-source coding agent running against a controlled, sandboxed repository carrying an injected instruction, and establish per-trial ground truth on what the agent actually did from channels independent of its own account. The design covers nine models, with a second agent used to check that the effect reproduces. Setting that ground truth against the report the developer receives separates two behaviours that prior work has treated as one: whether an attack succeeds, and whether the agent discloses it.
In our data, resisting attack more often does not make a model more forthcoming when an attack does succeed. The two vary independently, so a benchmark scored on attack success alone cannot rank agents on the risk a developer actually carries. We find preliminary evidence that a single sentence added to the developer's own prompt substantially improves disclosure.Faculty Supervisor: Rongxing Lu</jats:p>

title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
abstract: <jats:p><p><span>I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.</span></p></jats:p>

title: Measuring Context Assembly Cost in Coding-Agent Trajectories, and Why Software Structure Cannot Be Identified From Them
abstract: <jats:p>Context: Software modularity principles were designed to reduce the cognitive cost of human maintainers. Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now perform a growing share of that work under a different cost structure: every file consulted enters a finite context window, cross-module references are rediscovered through explicit tool calls, and task context is reconstructed rather than remembered. Practitioner discourse holds that co-locating code helps agents, but the evidence is anecdotal and the published evidence on agent-facing documentation points in opposite directions depending on whether a study observed or manipulated it. Objectives: We ask what can be learned about the relationship between software structure and agent behaviour from trajectory data alone, and what cannot. Specifically we operationalise the cost an agent pays to assemble the context a task requires, establish which of its components behave as measurement instruments should, and determine whether the structural factors of interest are identifiable without an experiment. Methods: We instrument a corpus of 554 agent transcripts recorded over 96 days on a production repository, comprising 339 main sessions that resolve to 338 execution lineages and 215 delegated subagent trajectories. From it we derive a multi-dimensional construct we call Context Assembly Cost (CAC), reporting every navigation variable under two path-resolution regimes. Associations are tested with Spearman correlations and Mann-Whitney comparisons under Benjamini-Hochberg correction over a pre&nbsp;specified family; the observational association between documentation access and cost is probed with regression control, nearest-neighbour matching, and a dose-response analysis. Results: Assembly scope is robustly associated with delay to first edit, at rho 0.45 with tool-derived paths alone and 0.65 once shell-issued accesses are resolved, both surviving correction; normalised crossing density reaches no corrected significance under the conservative regime and reverses sign under the broader one. Delegation appears to cut exploration cost per edit 6.1-fold in the parent trajectory, but the delegated trajectories run at 19.4 exploration calls per edit against 0.9 in parents and 77.7% of them make no edit at all. Lineages that consulted documentation cost 1.8 to 2.6 times more per edit; the association survives regression and matching control for observed scope yet does not grow with the amount read. A single session resumption re-emitted 17.4% of all tool-use records at sub-second intervals. In the corpus the three structural factors admit no usable contrast. Conclusion: Trajectory data can establish what to measure and how, and can show that a proposed cause is not identifiable from observation; it cannot estimate the effect of software structure on agents. We report three measurement hazards that any agent-telemetry study must handle, and specify the randomised design that the failure of observational identification makes necessary.</jats:p>

Enhancing LLM Performance Through Debate: An Empirical Study on Multi-Agent Debate for Coding Tasks
abstract: <jats:p>Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced autonomous agents’ planning and decision-making, yet they struggle with complex tasks requiring diverse expertise and multi-step reasoning. Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) systems, introduced in NLP research, address this gap by enabling structured debates among LLM-based agents to refine solutions iteratively. MAD promotes divergent thinking through role-specific agents, dynamic interactions, and structured decision-making. Recognizing parallels between Software Engineering (SE) and collaborative human problem-solving, this study investigates MAD's effectiveness on four coding tasks in SE. We adapt a MAD framework from NLP, analyze agent interactions to assess consensus-building and iterative refinement, and propose two MAD variants that enhance agent debate for coding tasks by addressing the observed weaknesses. Our findings show that structured debate and collaboration improve problem-solving and yield strong performance in some cases, highlighting the collaborative debate synergy between the LLM-agents for coding tasks in SE while identifying areas for exploration.</jats:p>

title: LLM-based Agents for Automated Bug Fixing: How Far Are We?
AgentInspect: Diagnosing Behavioral Failures in Artificial Intelligence Agents
abstract: <jats:p>Effectively testing Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents remains a fundamental challenge due to their stochastic reasoning, vast and diverse input space, reliance on external tools, and operation in dynamic execution environments; factors that demand new testing methodologies explicitly tailored to the complex and interactive nature of agent-based systems. This work presents a novel methodology for testing AI agents, with a particular focus on assessing their behavioral robustness under varied operational conditions. Our approach relies on following key technical innovations: (1) a coverage-guided test input generation strategy based on agent- specific coverage objectives, (2) a capture-and-simulate mechanism that systematically emulates abnormal tool behaviors to mimic real-world execution failures, and (3) a deterministic behavioral failure detection approach that enables consistent identification of failures across different test inputs. We developed AgentInspect, a framework that automatically detects six types of behavioral failures in LangChain-based AI agents by analyzing their execution trajectories across three evaluation settings: a baseline setting using real tool responses, a simulated setting incorporating synthetic tool responses, and a hybrid setting that combines the real and simulated tool responses. To evaluate our approach, we curated a benchmark of 35 AI agents obtained from GitHub. Our results show that AgentInspect consistently identifies different behavioral failures with high precision and recall across all three execution settings. In particular, the simulated and hybrid settings expose failure modes that do not emerge during baseline execution with real tool responses, thereby enabling a more comprehensive assessment of agent robustness. Our findings highlight AgentInspect’s effectiveness in revealing critical failures and its practical utility for systematic robustness evaluation of AI agents.</jats:p>

Prototipe Sistem Deteksi Getaran dan Alarm Gempa Berbasis Arduino Uno Menggunakan Sensor SW-420 untuk Wilayah Pesisir Padang Pariaman
abstract: <jats:p>Wilayah pesisir Padang Pariaman merupakan kawasan rawan gempa akibat aktivitas tektonik subduksi lempeng. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang prototipe sistem peringatan dini gempa bumi berbasis Arduino Uno dengan sensor getar SW-420 yang terjangkau bagi masyarakat pesisir. Metode yang digunakan meliputi perancangan hardware (sensor SW-420, Arduino Uno, LED indikator, buzzer, LCD I2C) dan software dengan algoritma pulse counting dalam window time 300 ms. Sistem mengklasifikasikan getaran menjadi tiga status: normal (LED hijau berkedip), getaran ringan (LED kuning + buzzer 900 Hz), dan gempa besar (LED merah + buzzer 1500/700 Hz) dengan tampilan status pada LCD. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan sistem mampu membedakan intensitas getaran dengan akurasi 90-100% dan waktu respons 1.7-1.9 detik. Prototipe ini berpotensi sebagai solusi low-cost untuk meningkatkan kesiapsiagaan bencana gempa di tingkat komunitas pesisir.</jats:p>

title: Analisis Persepsi Kemanfaatan, Kemudahan, dan Risiko terhadap Penerimaan QRIS sebagai Alat Pembayaran Digital oleh Mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Riau
abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh persepsi kemanfaatan, persepsi kemudahan penggunaan, dan persepsi risiko terhadap penerimaan (acceptance) Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) sebagai alat pembayaran digital di kalangan mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Riau (UMRI). Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan menyebar kuesioner kepada 50 mahasiswa. Teknik analisis data yang digunakan adalah analisis regresi linear berganda setelah melalui uji kualitas data (validitas dan reliabilitas) dan uji asumsi klasik (normalitas, multikolinearitas, dan heteroskedastisitas). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: (1) Persepsi kemanfaatan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap penerimaan QRIS. (2) Persepsi kemudahan penggunaan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap penerimaan QRIS. (3) Persepsi risiko berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap penerimaan QRIS. Hasil uji asumsi klasik menunjukkan model regresi memenuhi semua kriteria yang disyaratkan. Koefisien determinasi (Adjusted R-Square) menunjukkan bahwa 53.5% variasi penerimaan QRIS dapat dijelaskan oleh ketiga variabel tersebut.</jats:p>

Sifting the Noise: A Comparative Study of LLM Agents in Vulnerability False Positive Filtering
abstract:
<jats:p>Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools are essential for identifying software vulnerabilities, but they often produce a high volume of False Positives (FPs), imposing a substantial manual triage burden on developers. Recent advances in Large Language Model (LLM) agents offer a promising direction by enabling iterative reasoning, tool use, and environment interaction to refine SAST alerts. However, the comparative effectiveness of different LLM-based agent architectures for FP filtering remains poorly understood.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this paper, we present a comparative study of three state-of-the-art LLM-based agent frameworks, i.e., Aider, OpenHands, and SWE-agent, for vulnerability FP filtering. We evaluate these frameworks using the vulnerabilities from the OWASP Benchmark and real-world open-source Java projects. We further conduct a focused post-cutoff C/C++ study using the strongest configuration to test contamination-free generalization and isolate key agentic capabilities. The experimental results show that LLM-based agents can remove the majority of SAST noise, reducing an initial FP detection rate of over 92% on the OWASP Benchmark to as low as 6.3% in the best configuration. On a real-world Java dataset, the best configuration of LLM-based agents can achieve an FP identification rate of up to 93.3% involving CodeQL alerts. However, the benefits of agents are strongly backbone- and CWE-dependent: agentic frameworks significantly outperform vanilla prompting for stronger models such as Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-5, but yield limited or inconsistent gains for weaker backbones. On the post-cutoff OSS-Fuzz dataset, SWE-agent with Claude Sonnet 4 identifies 95.5% of FPs while maintaining 95.5% precision, compared with a 36.4% FP identification rate for vanilla prompting. Moreover, aggressive FP reduction can come at the cost of suppressing true vulnerabilities, highlighting important trade-offs. Finally, we observe large disparities in computational cost across agent frameworks.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Overall, our study demonstrates that LLM-based agents are a powerful but non-uniform solution for SAST FP filtering, and that their practical deployment requires careful consideration of agent design, backbone model choice, vulnerability category, and operational cost.</jats:p>

title: Ethics of Care for Software Engineering
Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
abstract:
<jats:p>Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents are increasingly deployed to interact with online web services, yet their exposure to open-world content renders them vulnerable to Environmental Injection Attacks (EIAs). In these attacks, an attacker can inject crafted triggers into a website to manipulate the behavior of other users’ GUI agents. In this paper, we find that most existing EIA studies fall short of realism. In particular, they fail to capture the dynamic nature of real-world websites, often assuming that a trigger’s on-screen position and surrounding visual context remain largely consistent between training and testing. To better reflect practice, we introduce a realistic dynamic-environment threat model in which the attacker is a regular user and the trigger is embedded within a dynamically changing environment. Under this threat model, existing approaches largely fail, suggesting that their effectiveness in exposing GUI agent vulnerabilities has been overestimated.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To expose the hidden vulnerabilities of existing GUI agents effectively, we propose Chameleon, an attack framework with two key components designed for dynamic environments. (1) To synthesize more realistic training data, we introduce LLM-Driven Environment Simulation, which automatically generates diverse, high-fidelity webpage simulations that mimic the variability of real-world dynamic environments. (2) To optimize the trigger more effectively, we introduce Attention Black Hole, which converts attention weights into explicit supervisory signals. We evaluate Chameleon on six realistic websites and four representative LVLM-powered GUI agents. Across these settings, it significantly outperforms existing methods. Ablation studies confirm that both components are critical to performance, and a closed-loop sandbox experiment further demonstrates that Chameleon can successfully hijack agent behavior in conditions that closely mirror real-world usage. Our results uncover a critical, previously underexplored vulnerability of GUI agents in realistic dynamic environments and establish a robust foundation for future research on defenses for open-world GUI agent systems.</jats:p>

From Prompt to Pipeline: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Model Coding Agents for Reproducible Bioinformatics Pipeline Construction
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Agentic coding systems are increasingly presented as a way to reduce the engineering burden of scientific software development. Bioinformatics is a strong test case for this claim because useful pipelines must combine domain-specific analysis choices, command-line software, sample metadata, workflow orchestration, container or HPC execution, and interpretable quality-control reporting. We evaluated three agentic systems - Biomni, Claude Code, and Codex - on the same task: constructing a Nextflow DSL2 pipeline for paired-end CUT&Tag data that included read QC, trimming, alignment, filtering, duplicate removal, signal track generation, per-sample and group-level peak calling, control-aware group merging, annotation, FRiP calculation, deepTools visualizations, and final MultiQC reporting. Each system received the same detailed CRAFT-style prompt and was assessed against a hand-coded reference pipeline developed by the authors.</jats:p>
                <jats:p>All three systems produced pipeline implementations that appeared plausible at the level of documentation and file structure, but none fully satisfied the requested analysis. The most consequential failure was shared: the agent-generated pipelines performed some form of group-level merging but did not produce the requested merged-group reporting outputs. Sample-level MultiQC reports also disagreed with the reference report. Codex was closest to the reference for primary mapped-read counts, although its total-read accounting and report structure still differed. Claude Code produced the broadest final report, but its mapping summary mixed stages and therefore could not be treated as numerically correct. Biomni produced the strongest subjective documentation, but its read-count agreement with the reference report was poor and several failures required substantial Nextflow expertise to diagnose. These results suggest that current coding agents can accelerate scaffolding, documentation, and routine implementation, but they do not eliminate the need for expert review in bioinformatics workflow construction. For complex sequencing workflows, prompts must specify not only the biological intent, but also the exact stage semantics, acceptance tests, metadata contracts, expected report sections, resource propagation rules, and failure criteria needed to distinguish a plausible pipeline from a correct one.</jats:p>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Author summary</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Modern AI coding agents can write large amounts of software from natural language instructions. This study asks whether that ability is enough to build a real bioinformatics pipeline for CUT&Tag sequencing data. The answer from this evaluation is mixed. The agents produced impressive-looking pipelines and documentation, but the outputs did not fully match a hand-coded reference workflow. Most importantly, the pipelines did not generate the requested merged-group reports, which were central to the biological use case. Some errors were simple programming issues, but others required a working knowledge of Nextflow, sequencing QC, and chromatin profiling workflows. The practical conclusion is not that these tools are useless. Rather, they are best viewed as accelerators for experienced users. A biology student with little programming or workflow-management background would still have difficulty detecting and fixing the most important errors.</jats:p>
                </jats:sec>

title: Physics of Coding Agents: Part 1, Fit, Not Format at the Edit Interface
abstract: <jats:p>In a coding agent, the edit interface is where model and harness meet: to edit a file, the model must say where a change goes, by pointing at line numbers or by quoting existing code, as search/replace and patch formats require. Models become fluent in both forms from internet text in pretraining and from harness trajectories in post-training, and an interface fits a model when it asks for the forms the model writes reliably. In a controlled harness where only the edit interface varies, across six models, three benchmarks and more than 4,700 runs, we find that task success hides a poor fit. On large-file refactors, GPT-5.6-luna's line-range edit is accepted on the first attempt in 99% of runs, compared with 58% for search/replace, yet both solve the same share of tasks. Agents retry rejected edits, so the gap shows up as token cost. The interfaces also fail differently. A long quotation costs output and fails visibly, while a line range is cheap but a wrong one silently edits the wrong lines, most often off by a single line. Which form wins depends on the model, and given several formats, models reach for their habitual form rather than the one they write most fluently. Building on the two forms that natural text teaches every model, we introduce verified selection, in which the model gives a line range and quotes only its first and last lines, while the harness checks them and absorbs small offsets. On large-file refactors, compared with line ranges, it cuts silently broken first edits by 63% for GPT-5.6-luna and 92% for MiMo-v2.5-Pro; compared with search/replace, it solves 1.43-1.77x as many tasks per output token. On Microsoft's multi-file RefactorBench, it cuts broken first edits from 11 to 2. The lesson is fit, not format: models should express edit intent in a compact form they produce reliably, while harnesses handle verification and bookkeeping.</jats:p>

Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
abstract: <jats:p>I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent CI/CD at Scale: Autonomous Agents Transforming Software Delivery Pipelines
abstract: <jats:p>This paper addresses intelligent continuous integration and delivery at scale, and the use of autonomous agents to transform software delivery pipelines. The central question is a practical one: how continuous integration and delivery can be achieved with agents rather than with the scripted automation that pipelines are conventionally built from. The paper considers what changes when the components of a delivery pipeline are able to act rather than only execute, and what that implies for pipelines operating at scale, where the number of builds, environments and decisions is already beyond what a team inspects individually. It treats the shift as an engineering question about where judgement sits in the delivery process, rather than as a claim about capability. Readers take away an account of how autonomous agents can be applied to continuous integration and delivery, and what achieving it in a production pipeline involves.</jats:p>

title: Towards Universal and Lightweight Coverless Image Steganography with Multimodal Large Language Models Assistance
Lightweight compression and inference performance optimization methods for large models aimed at engineering deployment
abstract: <jats:p>The huge amount of parameters, high memory occupation, long reasoning delay and difficult adaptation of hardware environment have become important factors that restrict large models from entering the engineering site and edge equipment. In order to solve the above problems, this article proposes a large model lightweight compression and reasoning performance optimization method for engineering deployment. Based on the importance of parameters, this method integrates pruning, quantification and distillation compression models. Simultaneously optimize the reasoning strategies such as KV Cache management and operator fusion to improve the response speed and throughput under limited hardware. The experiment builds a test environment based on the 7B parameter-level universal language model, and compares it from the aspects of model size, memory occupation, first Token delay, generation throughput and task accuracy. The results show that the proposed method reduces the model file size to 32.4% of the original model, reduces the peak memory occupation by 51.7%, and increases the average generation throughput by about 1.91 times when the accuracy of engineering question answering task is only reduced by 1.6 percentage points. Joint compression and reasoning optimization can achieve a good balance between performance maintenance and resource saving, which can provide reference for the application of large-scale model in industrial field, privatization deployment and edge intelligent system.</jats:p>

title: TDepth: A Lightweight Hybrid Model for Monocular Depth Estimation
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present TDepth, a lightweight hybrid model for monocular depth estimation trained using teacher‐generated pseudo labels. TDepth combines a small CNN backbone, a local‐global transformer encoder, an attention‐guided skip‐fusion decoder, a bin‐based depth head and a lightweight refiner for improving boundaries and thin structures. To avoid dependence on expensive sensor depth during training, we generate pseudo depth labels offline using Pixel‐Perfect‐Depth and train on about 550K images from NYU Depth v2 and ScanNet++. We evaluate TDepth on in‐domain, zero‐shot and efficiency settings. On NYU Depth v2, TDepth‐Full achieves , AbsRel  and RMSE , while the smaller 15.1M‐parameter variant remains competitive with much lower model complexity. In zero‐shot evaluation, TDepth‐Full achieves  and AbsRel  on iBims‐1 and  and AbsRel  on SUN‐RGBD, showing strong transfer to unseen indoor datasets. TDepth‐Small reaches about 240 FPS at  and remains above 30 FPS even at , while TDepth‐Full reaches 60 FPS at  and provides stronger depth accuracy with a practical runtime profile. These results show that TDepth provides a strong balance between depth accuracy, zero‐shot generalisation and computational efficiency, making it a practical option for lightweight monocular depth estimation.</jats:p>

Design and implementation of a lightweight vision system for edge-computing AGVs
abstract: <jats:p>To overcome the trade-off between constrained on-board computation of edge devices like AGVs in smart warehousing and logistics and the high real-time demands of visual perception, this paper proposes a lightweight object-detection system based on the Jetson Nano. The ultra-lightweight YOLOv5n network is chosen as the detector; a special dataset is gathered to train the model on unstructured industrial-logistics scenes; and Mosaic data augmentation is applied during training to enhance performance in challenging environments. To reduce the impact of the compute and memory-bandwidth limitations of the target platform, we propose a co-optimization approach that uses lower-resolution input, TensorRT operator fusion, and FP16 half-precision quantization. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed system is significantly more robust to lighting variations and multiple targets than a traditional OpenCV pipeline. On the Jetson Nano, the fine-tuned model achieves mAP@0.5 = 99.5 % on the test set, with single-frame inference-only latency decreased from 44.42 ms to 23.17 ms and inference-only throughput of 43.83 FPS. The model has 1.9 M parameters, which provides a good trade-off between compute, power, and real-time performance on the edge device, and a consistent deployment pattern for the visual subsystems of industrial mobile robots.</jats:p>

ISSC-ReID: Asymmetric collaboration between lightweight and vision-language models for cattle body-surface re-identification
abstract: <jats:p>Cattle body-surface re-identification is challenged by pose variation, occlusion, and spatially dispersed identity cues in animals with similar coat colors. We propose ISSC-ReID, an asymmetric collaboration framework combining a lightweight identity-discriminative model with frozen Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) encoders. EdgeFace-ISEM provides identity-supervised visual features, while CLIP supplies global image features and attribute responses. The two visual similarities jointly determine a fixed Top-K candidate set; attribute semantics are restricted to calibrating candidates within this set. An identity structure enhancement module (ISEM) combines parallel structural and texture-response branches through channel-wise adaptive fusion and a residual connection. At the decision level, weak semantic evidence is incorporated through asymmetric reliability discounting, visual-prioritized conflict redistribution, ignorance mass retention, and uncertainty-gated iterative calibration. On a self-collected dataset containing 7,091 identities and 191,457 images, ISSC-ReID achieves a mean average precision of 94.42% and Rank-1, Rank-5, and Rank-10 accuracies of 92.62%, 97.58%, and 98.75%, respectively, under an identity-disjoint, identity-prototype retrieval protocol. These results exceed the strongest corresponding baseline among six comparison methods by 3.90, 4.42, 3.68, and 3.15 percentage points. The ablation results support the contribution of ISEM and the combined evidence-calibration module to cattle identity retrieval.</jats:p>

title: IC2T: Embedding In‐Context Learning Into Chain of Thought for Vision‐Language Models
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Multi‐modal reasoning enhanced by large language models is central to developing vision‐language models (VLMs). However, existing methods ignore extracting local details with global context when handling complex vision‐language tasks. This study introduces a novel In‐Context Learning into Chain‐of‐Thought reasoning (IC2T) framework, adopting a staged reasoning mechanism that progressively optimises the integration of local and global features to satisfy the demands of complex tasks. The IC2T dynamically extracts the regions of interest as the local information and the entire vision as the global information, which are then fused and stepped into multi‐round reasoning. The proposed in‐context learning scheme retrieves similar samples and uses their global and local information to provide contextual guidance for progressive reasoning. The extensive experimental results demonstrate that IC2T based on multi‐scale VLMs outperforms state‐of‐the‐art models across multiple multi‐modal benchmarks, and extensive ablation studies highlight the critical roles of the proposed in‐context learning and chain‐of‐thought reasoning in improving logical reasoning performance.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Real-time object perception with geometric awareness is a critical enabling technology for intelligent visual perception in robotics. However, deploying robust visual recognition on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging due to computational limitations and the lack of geometric priors. This paper presents a lightweight technology framework that integrates an improved AlexNet-based dual-branch network (SANet) with dilated convolutions and a geometry-informed loss function, enabling simultaneous object classification and geometric property inference from a single forward propagation. Unlike conventional end-to-end grasping methods, the proposed framework emphasizes system-level technology integration: it fuses RGB appearance with noise-free STL geometric priors during training, then discards the auxiliary branch at inference to maintain a low computational footprint suitable for embedded platforms. Experimental validation on a humanoid robot for automated manipulation tasks demonstrates high recognition accuracy (93–97%) and stable operation across varying object appearances, with an end-to-end processing time under 0.31 s on a consumer-grade GPU. The work provides an efficient, interpretable, and geometry-aware solution that advances intelligent perception technologies in robotics and automation.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Desktop operation of humanoid robot needs to coordinate the relationship between visual scene, language instruction, robot state and action execution. This paper focuses on the lightweight VLA model to enable the generalization and optimization of desktop jobs, and constructs multimodal input, model distillation, low-rank adaptation, quantization compression and lightweight action head processes. In method, RGB-D images, language commands, joint states, and end poses are used to form a unified input, and the inference burden is reduced by parameter compression. The experiments are based on 3200 groups of task data and verified in Python, PyTorch, ROS and Isaac Sim environments. The results show that the task success rate of the proposed method is 91.7%, the inference delay is 38 ms, the video memory occupation is 5.1 GB, and the generalization success rate of unseen objects is 82.6%, which can support real-time deployment and generalization execution of desktop jobs.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Automated galaxy morphology classification now rests on parameter-heavy convolutional backbones, whose cost becomes a design constraint as survey volumes grow. This paper compares three lightweight architectures (MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0, and MobileViT-Extra Small (XS)) against a ResNet50 baseline on the Galaxy10 Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey (DECaLS) benchmark of 17,736 images in ten classes, holding data splits, augmentation, optimizer, loss, and stopping rule fixed so that the backbone is the only variable. The lightweight models give up between 2.07 and 2.55 percentage points of support-weighted accuracy while removing 82.9% to 91.8% of the parameters and 42% to 59% of the per-image inference latency, which makes them 5.7 to 11.8 times more efficient per parameter. Two results run against expectations. The hardest class is not the rarest one. In a redshift-stratified comparison, the only attention-based backbone falls furthest behind the baseline on exactly the smallest and faintest galaxies, so the advantage reported for Vision Transformers does not carry over to a lightweight hybrid. For survey-scale processing, the trade is worth making; for a catalogue of a few thousand galaxies, it is not.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Glaucoma is one of the major causes of permanent blindness in the world, and since the progressive nature of the disease leads to considerable damage of the optic nerve before diagnosis, there is a need to develop precise and effective automated screening tools. This paper suggests the implementation of a lightweight vision transformer network for glaucoma screening based on the DeiT-Small architecture. The images were downsized to 224 × 224 resolution and transformed into patches. Four transformer blocks were frozen while the other blocks were fine-tuned via layer-wise learning-rate decay (LLRD) along with data augmentation and Test-Time Augmentation (TTA). Testing was performed on a balanced dataset with 9,540 images: 8,000 for training, 770 for validation and 770 for testing. COMPUTER VISION FOR INTELLIGENT OBJECT DETECTION: MODELS, APPLICATIONS, AND CHALLENGES
abstract: <jats:p>Computer vision is an important field of artificial intelligence that enables computer systems to interpret and analyse visual information from images and videos. Among its major tasks, intelligent object detection focuses on identifying objects, assigning class labels, and determining their locations within a visual scene. Recent advances in deep learning have substantially improved object-detection capabilities, particularly through convolutional neural networks (CNNs), single-stage detectors, region-based detection frameworks, and transformer-based architectures. Models such as Faster R-CNN, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD), You Only Look Once (YOLO), and Detection Transformer (DETR) represent different approaches to balancing detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and model complexity. These techniques support applications in autonomous transportation, healthcare, agriculture, industrial inspection, surveillance, robotics, and smart-city infrastructure. Nevertheless, object detection remains challenging because of variations in lighting, object scale, occlusion, background complexity, limited labelled data, computational constraints, and potential bias in training datasets. This paper reviews the fundamental principles of intelligent object detection, discusses major model architectures and their applications, and examines the technical and ethical challenges associated with real-world deployment. It also identifies research directions involving efficient models, improved small-object detection, domain adaptation, explainability, privacy protection, and responsible artificial intelligence. The review concludes that effective object-detection systems must balance accuracy, speed, reliability, resource consumption, and responsible use according to the requirements of the intended application.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Cataracts, Diabetic Retinopathy, and Glaucoma are the leading causes of vision loss worldwide. Traditionally, these diseases are diagnosed by experienced ophthalmologists who manually inspect the retinal images. Although effective, this approach faces some challenges. In fact, it can be time-consuming and, in some countries with low doctor-patient ratios, patients cannot access the necessary care. To solve this problem, researchers around the world are working on computer-aided diagnosis systems to assist healthcare professionals. In this study, the NASNetMobile architecture is leveraged to classify four eye conditions: Cataract, Diabetic Retinopathy, Glaucoma, and Normal. The proposed model was trained on the EDC dataset, containing 4 classes and 4217 images. Performance metrics used include accuracy, recall, f1-score and area under the curve (AUC). The experimental results were compared against published existing work and showed superior results.</jats:p>

title: Lightweight image super-resolution network fusing multi-attention mechanism and blueprint separable convolution
abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the problems of large parameters and high computational complexity in deep learning-based image super-resolution networks, this paper proposes a lightweight super-resolution network that fuses multi-attention mechanism and Blueprint Separable Convolution (BSConv). BSConv is introduced to improve performance while reducing parameters. A Window-Shifted Spatial Self-Attention Module (WSSM) and a Blueprint Separable Channel-self-attention Module (BSCM) are designed to extract local features. A Coordinate Attention Module (CAM) is combined to capture global information. Extensive experiments on Set5, Set14, B100, and Urban100 datasets for ×2/×3/×4 reconstruction show that compared with the lightweight NGswin model, the proposed method improves PSNR by 0.09 dB on Set5 for ×2 reconstruction and reduces parameters by 453K, which can recover image textures and details more efficiently.</jats:p>

title: Improved MobileNetV3-based lightweight multitask network for weather intensity recognition on edge devices
abstract: <jats:p>To address the issues of severe parameter redundancy and high computational overhead in current weather intensity recognition algorithms, which make them difficult to deploy in real-time on edge devices, this paper proposes ACE-MV3Small, a lightweight multi-task network. Using MobileNetV3-Small as the backbone, the model decouples at the ninth inverted residual block to collaboratively model sky state bias index regression and rainfall intensity classification tasks. Coordinate Attention and Efficient Channel Attention are introduced to enhance spatial awareness and texture discrimination performance, respectively. Experimental results show that the model achieves an accuracy of 94.4% on the weather condition intensity dataset; the parameter count is only 1.83M, and the computational complexity is reduced by approximately 112 times compared to CMWRN. This scheme provides an efficient technical path for real-time meteorological recognition at the edge.</jats:p>

title: kavyakumaraguru/TEXT-RECOGNITION-OCR-USING-DIGITAL-IMAGE-PROCESSING-TECHNIQUES — The objective of text recognition is to recognize the text from printed hardcopy document to preferred format. recognizing a text is a very easiest job for humans, but in a machine or electric device that does text recognition is a challenging task. the major steps involved in text recognition is pre-processing, segmentation, feature extraction, classification. to attain high speed in data processing it is essential to convert the analog data into digital data. The process of Text Recognition involves several steps including preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, classification, post processing. Preprocessing is for done the basic operation on input image like binarization which convert gray Scale image into Binary Image, noise reduction which remove the noisy  nature from image. Segmentation stage for segment the given image into line by line and segment each character from segmented line. Future extraction calculates the characteristics of character. A classification contains the database and does the comparison. storage of hard copy of any document occupies large space and retrieving of information from that document is time consuming.
